abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of deep learning has significantly advanced vision-based structural health monitoring (SHM), enabling automated inspection and condition assessment. However, most existing models remain purely data-driven and lack mechanisms to quantify predictive confidence, limiting their reliability in safety-critical applications. This study introduces a deep Bayesian learning framework using fully convolutional DenseNet (FC-DenseNet) to integrate uncertainty quantification into vision-based SHM tasks. By leveraging Monte Carlo dropout, predictive entropy, and class softmax standard deviation, the proposed approach not only enhances segmentation performance but also generates pixel-level uncertainty maps. To address challenges in interpreting these outputs, two surrogate models are introduced: Uncertainty -Assisted Segmentation (UAS) for refining predictions and Prediction Quality Tagging (PQT) for flagging potentially unreliable outputs. The framework is validated across three case studies binary crack detection, damage localization, and multiclass bridge component recognition using real-world datasets. Results demonstrate that Bayesian inference combined with surrogate models outperforms conventional dropout approaches in terms of accuracy, F1-score, and intersection over union (IoU). Moreover, the proposed PQT mechanism provides a practical safeguard for high-risk applications by alerting human operators to uncertain predictions. The findings highlight the potential of Bayesian deep learning to improve the robustness, interpretability, and trustworthiness of automated SHM systems.</jats:p>
title: Deep vision techniques for structural health monitoring Uncertainty in condition
